newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Aug CPI rose 1.33 percent - Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Aug CPI rose 1.33 percent - Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 1.33 percent in August from the month before after rising 1.42 percent in July, Banco de Mexico said.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 1.23 percent in August from the month before, compared to rise of 1.24 percent in July.
The central bank said that compared with the same month a year earlier the CPI was 30.6 percent higher.
The accumulated inflation rate for the first eight months of the year was 18.50 percent, compared with 37.88 percent in the same period a year earlier.
It said that the main causes of inflation this month were increases in rent, eggs, beans, domestic gas, soaps and detergents, medicines, oranges, onions, gasoline and cigarettes.
It said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 1.61 percent in August from the month before.
A survey of 13 Mexican brokerages and research companies found expectations of a rise of 1.36 percent for August's CPI.
Banco de Mexico gave the following breakdown for August:
INDEX Percent
Food, drinks and tobacco 1.18
Clothing and shoes 1.71
Housing 1.42
Furniture 2.13
Health and personal care 1.54
Transportation 1.03
Education 1.51
Other services 0.91
In August, the producer price index, excluding petroleum, was 30.06 percent higher than the same month a year earlier.
The accumulated increase for the first eight months was 17.0 percent.
In the first eight months of 1995, the index rose an accumulated 41.14 percent, Banco de Mexico said.
